articles.excerpt: 💡 What I Built THE LAST PROCESS is a 100% pure, native terminal horror game built in Python using rich and prompt_toolkit. It connects to local open-weight models via Ollama (e.g. gemma:2b, llama3.2,…
articles.body: 💡 What I Built THE LAST PROCESS is a 100% pure, native terminal horror game built in Python using rich and prompt_toolkit . It connects to local open-weight models via Ollama (e.g. gemma:2b , llama3.2 , or mistral ) to give life to Entity 0 —an evasive heuristic monitor trapped in an abandoned research station console. What if closing a terminal didn't mean the thing inside it was gone? Meet THE LAST PROCESS — a psychological horror game that turns an ordinary terminal into an abandoned research station, where something is watching, responding, and slowly revealing that you might not be who you think you are. 👁️ Welcome to Project Erebos You enter Terminal Bay 3 as an operator investigating an abandoned research facility. At first, everything seems normal.

articles.title: On-Device Semantic Retrieval on iOS: How Lumo Solves Note Fatigue Without Cloud Latency
articles.excerpt: When building personal AI productivity tools, most products follow a lazy cloud-first pattern: For developers and privacy-conscious professionals, this pattern is a dealbreaker: Network Latency: You s…
articles.body: When building personal AI productivity tools, most products follow a lazy cloud-first pattern: Every keystroke or audio chunk is shipped across the public internet to an unvetted cloud endpoint, processed through heavy remote pipelines, and pushed back after a 2-second roundtrip. For developers and privacy-conscious professionals, this pattern is a dealbreaker: Network Latency: You shouldn't have to wait for an internet handshake just to capture a quick epiphany in an elevator or on a flight. Data Confidentiality: Architecture trade-offs, private bug post-mortems, and customer feedback should not sit unencrypted on a third-party server. When designing Lumo (Memory Copilot) , we chose a fundamentally different engineering path: local-first semantic retrieval .

articles.title: A one-page checklist for testing one AI workflow before handoff
articles.excerpt: A small team does not need a program to hand off an AI workflow. It needs one workflow, a few honest tests and a person who can run them without the builder in the room. Here is the checklist I would…
articles.body: A small team does not need a program to hand off an AI workflow. It needs one workflow, a few honest tests and a person who can run them without the builder in the room. Here is the checklist I would use. The example is a hypothetical demo, not client work: an assistant that reads a shared support inbox and drafts replies for a person to review. Pick one bounded workflow Write one sentence that says what it does and what it does not do. "It drafts replies to support emails. It never sends them." If you cannot write that sentence, the workflow is not ready to hand off. Run the checks Keep the list short enough that someone will actually use it. Test with ordinary input. Run ten real-looking messages through it. Read every draft. Do not skim. Test with bad input.

articles.title: Forced SSH commands still need a complete key policy
articles.excerpt: Forced SSH commands still need a complete key policy An authorized_keys entry can restrict a public key to a fixed command, disable terminal allocation, and turn off forwarding features. These options…
articles.body: Forced SSH commands still need a complete key policy An authorized_keys entry can restrict a public key to a fixed command, disable terminal allocation, and turn off forwarding features. These options are useful for backup agents, deployment hooks, and narrow administrative paths. They are not a complete authorization system by themselves. The command, the key's owner, the environment it inherits, and the server configuration all affect what the key can actually do. The OpenSSH restrict option is a convenient starting point because it disables several interactive and forwarding features. A hard-coded command= option then supplies the command to run when the key authenticates.

Modern Warfare 4, developed by Infinity Ward, thrusts players into the forefront of a North Korean invasion of South Korea. A video of real life rescue efforts from the crush in Itaewon, which led to the death of almost 160 people, appears briefly in Modern Warfare 4’s opening montage. According to the BBC , the families issued a statement saying they were “appalled” that the footage was used in the game, and demanded Activision pull it.

articles.title: Causal Discovery: Why Conditional Independence Can Recover a Graph - and When It Cannot
articles.excerpt: Correlation tells you that two variables move together. It does not tell you why. Causal discovery is the attempt to go one step further: given observational data alone, can we recover the causal grap…
articles.body: Correlation tells you that two variables move together. It does not tell you why. Causal discovery is the attempt to go one step further: given observational data alone, can we recover the causal graph that generated it? Sometimes the answer is yes, up to an important qualification. Sometimes it is no, and the reason is instructive. This article explains the core idea, the assumptions it rests on, the most widely used algorithm, and the pitfalls that make practitioners overclaim. The question, stated precisely Assume the data come from a causal directed acyclic graph, a DAG. Each node is a variable. Each directed edge means a direct causal effect.
articles.author: Umesh Tharuka Malaviarachchi

articles.title: How an Eventually Consistent DynamoDB GSI Let Mobile Retries Create 1,400 Duplicate Orders
articles.excerpt: 14:07 UTC. PagerDuty fires on fulfillment-queue-depth, 340% of baseline and climbing. Checkout's on-call pulls up the dashboard expecting a stuck consumer or a slow downstream call. Instead she finds…
articles.body: 14:07 UTC. PagerDuty fires on fulfillment-queue-depth , 340% of baseline and climbing. Checkout's on-call pulls up the dashboard expecting a stuck consumer or a slow downstream call. Instead she finds the queue isn't slow, it's just full of orders nobody placed twice on purpose. the scramble First theory: the mobile app's retry logic, rewritten three weeks ago to handle flaky connections more aggressively, is double-submitting. Someone pulls the client-side request logs for a sample of the duplicate order IDs. Each one shows exactly one tap, one request, one Idempotency-Key header generated client-side and reused correctly across any retries the client itself issued. The client is behaving. Ruled out in under five minutes.

articles.excerpt: Even emergency calls aren't safe from this silent threat.
articles.body: TL;DR A newly disclosed Android vulnerability allows malicious text messages to silently crash a phone’s calling service, potentially interrupting emergency calls. Repeated messages can trigger persistent crashes and reboot loops, making affected devices hard to recover without technical help. Google developed a fix months before the public disclosure, but questions remain about when users will receive the patch. Imagine dialing 911, only for your phone to suddenly drop the call . You haven’t pressed anything, your signal hasn’t disappeared, and there’s no obvious explanation. Somewhere in the background, however, a text message you never received has just brought your phone’s calling service to its knees.

articles.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
articles.excerpt: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the JWST, if it wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface.
articles.body: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere.
articles.author: Robert Lea

articles.title: Patrick Stewart, renowned actor and ‘Star Trek’s’ Captain Picard, dies at 86
articles.excerpt: Patrick Stewart, the distinguished British actor of stage and screen, passed away Wednesday (Oct. 28) in Los Angeles at the age of 86.
articles.body: Less than a week after the fates took Walter Koenig from our galaxy, another " Star Trek " legend has left us: Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. According to his spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, the beloved Shakespearean actor passed away on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at his Los Angeles home after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Bush Novak shared.

articles.body: Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini . The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now.
